Use case: scientific-educational, children's picture-book illustration.
Asset type: landscape 3:2 illustration for a Chinese parent-and-child microbiology website.
Create a richly painted, concrete, warm educational illustration about bread yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), with handmade watercolor and colored-pencil detail, credible forms, soft natural light, cream paper, no typography.
Scene: a home kitchen tabletop, a glass bowl of risen bread dough with visible gas bubbles in a small cutaway section, a loaf cut open showing the porous crumb, a small dish of food-grade yeast. One large illustrated circular magnified inset occupies about one third of the canvas and clearly shows oval yeast cells, including a mother cell with a smaller attached bud. Render yeast as real rounded cell shapes, no faces, eyes, arms, mouths or magical glow. The microscopic inset is explicitly a visual cutaway/magnification convention, not microorganisms floating full-size in the kitchen. Children should recognize the bread immediately and see where the bubbles are. Coherent picture-book scene, not generic icons, not flat SVG, not a clinical 3D render. Spacious composition, all principal objects fully in frame. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, logos, watermark, ruler or scale bar. No children handling raw dough, no tasting raw flour.

Subject and scientific requirements: An inviting breakfast table: plain yogurt in a ceramic bowl with a spoon holding thick yogurt, a small clear glass of milk, a parent and child looking at the yogurt together. Magnified inset: several short chains of rounded Streptococcus thermophilus bacterial cells, pearly pale-gold cells, no nuclei inside bacteria. The lesson is milk turning into yogurt, not milk left to spoil.

Subject and scientific requirements: A sunlit pond edge with freshwater plants, a parent and child looking through a small field microscope at a prepared slide on a dry stable table, no collection or culturing. Large circular magnified inset shows a single Paramecium caudatum, elongated slipper-shaped cell entirely edged with many very short cilia, a visible oral groove along one side, a kidney-like macronucleus, rounded internal food vacuoles and a star-shaped contractile vacuole. Several tiny bacterial particles near the oral groove show its food. No animal face, no legs, no long tail flagellum, no eyes. Water and light reflections are recognizable; the microbe only appears in the magnified inset.
